_model.mc-serial: mc, examples/api shape: 1 process, 1 thread, one connection at a time, no keep-alive (Connection: close)
_model.mc-fork1: mc, registry (mcweb) shape: parent accepts, fork() per connection, child answers ONE request and _exit()s (Connection: close), waitpid(WNOHANG) reap, <= 64 live workers
_model.mc-forkka: mc, fork() per connection with keep-alive: child loops over requests until the client closes; same parent as fork1
_model.c-serial: C raw sockets: 1 process, 1 thread, one connection at a time, no keep-alive (the mc-serial shape)
_model.go-nethttp: Go net/http: goroutine per connection, keep-alive, GOMAXPROCS=10
_model.rust-threads: Rust std::net blocking, one OS thread per connection, keep-alive, no crates
_model.zig-threads: Zig 0.16 std.Io.net (Threaded Io), one OS thread per connection, keep-alive
_model.cs-jit: C# ASP.NET Core minimal API on Kestrel, `dotnet cs.dll` (JIT, shared runtime), thread pool + async I/O, keep-alive
_model.cs-aot: C# same program published NativeAOT (-p:PublishAot=true), Kestrel, thread pool + async I/O, keep-alive

_runtime.go-nethttp: Go runtime, statically linked into the binary
_runtime.cs-jit: .NET 10 CLR + ASP.NET Core shared framework, loaded at run time (106 MiB under libexec/shared)
_runtime.cs-aot: NativeAOT: runtime + GC + Kestrel compiled into the binary; dylibs: libssl/libcrypto (Homebrew), brotli, ICU, Swift/Foundation
